record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: In the one-dimensional positive-density Lieb-Thirring inequality at γ=1, a logarithmic correction term is currently needed. Is that correction really necessary, or does the inequality already hold without it for every γ>1?

evidence.quote: Moreover, for γ = 1 in d = 1 the inequality holds only with a logarithmic correction term. Does the inequality hold without this term for γ > 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider the Schrödinger operator $-\Delta + V$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ is a real-valued potential with $V_- = \max(-V,0) \in L^{\gamma+d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. The classical Lieb–Thirring inequality bounds sums of moments of negative eigenvalues. There is a "positive-density" analogue which controls perturbations of the Fermi sea: for a density parameter $\rho>0$, one studies operators of the form $-\Delta - \mu + V$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $\mu = (2\pi\rho)^{2}$ in $d=1$, suitably normalized), and one seeks inequalities estimating
$$\mathrm{Tr}\bigl[(-\Delta-\mu+V)_-^{\gamma}\bigr] - \mathrm{Tr}\bigl[(-\Delta-\mu)_-^{\gamma}\bigr]$$
in terms of an integral of $V$ (e.g. $\int |V|^{\gamma+1/2}$ in $d=1$, plus possibly lower-order terms involving $V$).

Known fact in $d=1$, $\gamma=1$. In one space dimension at the endpoint exponent $\gamma=1$, the positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality is currently established only with an additional logarithmic correction term on the right-hand side (a term involving a logarithm of an $L^p$-norm of $V$).

Problem. Determine whether for every $\gamma > 1$ in dimension $d=1$ the positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality holds without any logarithmic correction term; equivalently, prove or disprove that for every $\gamma>1$ there exists a finite constant $C=C(\gamma)$ such that
$$\mathrm{Tr}\bigl[(-\Delta-\mu+V)_-^{\gamma}\bigr] - \mathrm{Tr}\bigl[(-\Delta-\mu)_-^{\gamma}\bigr] \le C\int_{\mathbb{R}} |V(x)|^{\gamma+1/2}\,dx$$
for all admissible real potentials $V$ and all $\mu>0$, with no additional logarithmic factor.
artifact.status_search_result: The positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality was established by Frank, Lewin, Lieb, and Seiringer (Duke Math. J., 2013), with a logarithmic correction necessary at the endpoint $\gamma=1$ in $d=1$. Recent surveys (2022) still list as open whether the logarithmic correction can be removed for all $\gamma>1$ in one dimension; no resolution was found in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: A positive density analogue of the Lieb-Thirring inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Frank, Lewin, Lieb, Seiringer establish the positive-density Lieb-Thirring inequality, with a logarithmic correction needed in d=1 at gamma=1.
status_evidence.claim: The positive-density Lieb-Thirring inequality is proved with a logarithmic correction at the endpoint exponent in 1D.

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on Lieb-Thirring inequalities, including the question whether logarithmic corrections in the positive-density case can be removed.
status_evidence.claim: The removal of the logarithmic correction in the 1D positive-density Lieb-Thirring inequality is listed as an open problem.
